title: Understand Conatus installation and scheduled activation
summary: Read matched release selection, explicit product maintenance, independent update and email schedules, failure halts and installation instruction behavior.
use_when: Release, provider, maintenance, schedule identity, activation, deployment or scheduling failure behavior must be understood.
do_not_use_when: The request needs source capture, Annals interpretation or email submission semantics alone.
A selected executable or catalog entry is being treated as proof of readiness or domain success.
outcome: The selected release, maintenance or scheduled activation boundary is understood independently of domain outcomes.
effects: Installation selects a immutable executable and matching complete provider bundle; it initializes no state or schedule.
Definition generation writes a new immutable definition and private logs directory without registration or activation.

Explicit maintenance holds durable admission. The deploy instruction publishes programs, initializes absent state or updates the Annals path and publishes each selected runner with its intended enabled state under ordinary admission and runner locks.
authority: Conatus owns installation selection, product maintenance, generated definitions and output. Clockwork owns registration, activation and incidents. Annals and Email own their domain readiness and outcomes.
success: Selection metadata identifies the packaged release. Binding and history observations establish activation; Conatus receipts separately establish domain work.
failure_and_recovery: Stop on conflicting selectors, failed setup or unresolved admission. Recover an exact retained release and release only the operation's own hold.
Clockwork scheduling incidents require explicit continuation approval. Deployment, definition switch and Conatus resume cannot clear an incident or retry failed domain work.
privacy: Installer and schedule definitions use local current-user paths and no credential. Private sources, email occurrences, logs and context retain their existing product owners; no cleanup policy is supplied.
does_not_authorize: Live activation without intended binding authority, personal email without explicit or standing authority, clearing failure incidents, another owner hold release, domain rollback, credential changes or cleanup.

consumers.statement: Local operators and deployment coordinators need release, maintenance and scheduled activation behavior.

preconditions.statement: Installation requires exact candidate binary and matching bundle, the expected current selection and current-user owned paths. Definition generation requires selected installed release, existing state and output parent and a new output file. Activation separately needs initialized product state, ready dependencies and intended schedule authority.

inputs.statement: Installation selects exact binary, bundle and expected current; --home selects another home. Recovery selects one retained release. Definitions select absolute state and output with optional --daily-email. Maintenance uses an exact owner. Deployment settings select absolute paths, library and independent update/email enabled intent.

outputs.statement: Commands print readable text by default. --json selects the existing {ok:true,data:...} machine response. Human and JSON errors go to stderr with a nonzero exit; JSON errors retain {ok:false,error:string}. Packaging reports release selection without state-integrity, artifact-integrity, or readiness checks. Definition receipts identify key, release and path with registered:false and activated:false. Config exposes dependency and library selections; maintenance reports admission and drain. Ordinary config and maintenance commands use readable labeled text by default. Separate conatus-install and deployment machine responses are unchanged.

data_semantics.statement: Installed program and provider share an immutable release, with bundle bytes included in identity. A definition pins that release. Selection is not readiness; activation and exit-zero process are not domain success.

identity_and_units.statement: Default install root is ~/Library/Application Support/Conatus/install. Expected current is absent or releases/ID. Update key conatus/update uses 300 seconds and run-at-load. Email key conatus/daily-email uses local 09:00, no run-at-load and 180-second activation limit. Both use schema-two halt-until-approved and overlap skip.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Inspect describes selected release metadata. Installation reads existing bindings to preserve their intended selections and enabled state. Clockwork history describes activations while Conatus receipts describe domain work.
No maximum activation delay, catch-up guarantee or domain completion time is promised.

access.statement: Current-user local installer owns Conatus release and provider selection. --home selects packaging root. Conatus local maintenance uses private state and owner-scoped durable holds; documentation presence grants no execution authority.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Direct installation initializes no state and changes no active schedule. Recovery selects an exact retained release without reverting domain state or Clockwork bindings. Definition generation does not register or activate.

An abend ends the current run for either schema-two binding. Clockwork permits later activations before its shared service-health threshold. By default, five consecutive failed read-only checks, at least 60 seconds apart, establish the halt and alert eligibility together. Healthy or inactive checks clear a pending episode. An established halt requires exact approval. Product pause, Annals pause, incidents and email uncertainty remain independent. Deliberate scheduled admission during maintenance is a successful skip.

The declared deploy instruction publishes programs, initializes absent state or updates the final Annals executable while preserving library identities, cursor, records, instructions and pause. Existing library selections cannot change. Each selected binding retains its timer, arguments, environment and output paths; the executable and Clockwork pin change to the new selection with intended enabled state. No maintenance hold, schedule suspension, drain, health check or signature audit occurs. Existing incidents remain in force.

Optional settings state_dir, decisions_config and annals_state_dir are absolute; library and separate enabled/daily_email_enabled select intent. Fresh defaults use installed Annals state, decisions/config.toml and library conatus. An absent binding remains absent unless its enabled setting is supplied; omitted email intent preserves prior selection and intent. Failure leaves completed effects in place. Interruption requires inspection and an explicit next operation, without automatic replay, rollback or recovery.

operational_limits.statement: Installation, initialization, schedule registration and activation are separate effects. Both bindings skip overlap; email has a 180-second activation limit. Product release recovery does not revert databases, Annals or frozen email bytes.
No general installation latency, history retention, throughput or storage capacity guarantee is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Provider schema 4 adds the product overview. Conatus state remains schema 1. Older releases can ignore want archive markers; retained email occurrences preserve historical bytes. Schema-one Clockwork bindings acquire failure halt policy only after explicit schema-two selection.
No general cross-release support or deprecation interval is promised.

Contract 4 requires --json for the ordinary CLI machine response. The prior JSON success and error shapes and their streams are preserved with that flag. Default readable text does not change persistent state formats or the separate installation and status-snapshot protocols.

reliances.statement: Clockwork registers exact immutable definitions, activates both bindings and owns scheduling incidents and notification.
